about: The four readers of a report's layout must agree, and where they do not today the difference is pinned as `knownDifference` rather than fixed. `layoutCases`: `compiled` is the server's compiled-notes reader (`factsCarryArtifactTag`/`factsLayout` over a compiled model, the path discovery takes), `text` the raw-text reader (`textClaimsToBeAReport`/`layoutOfText`, for a file that did not compile and for text the write path is handed), `lint` the layout `lintNotebookText` lints the file as, and `sdk` the builder's reader (`readDashboardDocument`): `grid`, `linear`, `null` for not a report, or `refused` for a tag the SDK will not open. `queryTagCases` pin the three detectors of a deprecated query-level `# artifact`: `compiled` (`queryNotesCarryArtifact` over the file's own named queries), `text` (`QUERY_ARTIFACT_NOTE`, read as `layoutFactsOfText(…).queryTag`) and `lint` (whether `lintNotebookText` reads the file, which has no model-level tag, as a report). The server's spec reads the server columns (report_layout_parity.spec.ts) and the SDK's spec the `sdk` column (readDocument.spec.ts); each also fails when a case's readers differ and it carries no `knownDifference`.

layoutCases.name: `layout=grid` with tiles is grid
layoutCases.source:
## artifact { layout=grid tiles=["s -> v"] }
source: s is duckdb.sql("select 1 as x") extend { view: v is { group_by: x } }

layoutCases.name: `layout=linear` with no tiles is linear
the legacy `kind=dashboard` is grid
layoutCases.source:
## artifact { kind=dashboard tiles=["s -> v"] }
source: s is duckdb.sql("select 1 as x") extend { view: v is { group_by: x } }

layoutCases.name: the legacy `kind=notebook` is linear
a tag naming no layout and listing no tiles is linear by default
a tiles list with no layout is grid
layoutCases.source:
## artifact { tiles=["s -> v"] }
source: s is duckdb.sql("select 1 as x") extend { view: v is { group_by: x } }

layoutCases.name: a `dashboard { … }` grid tag on the artifact line is grid
layoutCases.source:
## artifact { } dashboard { columns=6 }
source: s is duckdb.sql("select 1 as x") extend { view: v is { group_by: x } }

layoutCases.name: a `## dashboard { … }` grid tag on its own line, with no layout, kind or tiles
layoutCases.knownDifference: The compiled reader and the lint read every model-level note, so the separate grid tag makes it grid; the text reader and the SDK read only the artifact tag's own note, so it is linear. Pinned: a refactor that unifies the readers must keep both answers.

layoutCases.name: `layout=linear` wins over a tiles list
layoutCases.source:
## artifact { layout=linear tiles=["s -> v"] }
source: s is duckdb.sql("select 1 as x") extend { view: v is { group_by: x } }

layoutCases.name: `layout=grid` wins over a disagreeing `kind=notebook`
layoutCases.source:
## artifact { layout=grid kind=notebook }
source: s is duckdb.sql("select 1 as x") extend { view: v is { group_by: x } }

layoutCases.name: an unknown `layout=` falls through to the tiles list
layoutCases.source:
## artifact { layout=wide tiles=["s -> v"] }
source: s is duckdb.sql("select 1 as x") extend { view: v is { group_by: x } }

layoutCases.name: a `##|` block tag is read like a one-line tag
a model-level tag that does not parse
layoutCases.source:
## artifact { layout=grid tiles=[ }
source: s is duckdb.sql("select 1 as x") extend { view: v is { group_by: x } }
layoutCases.knownDifference: Compiled, an unparsable tag carries no `artifact` property, so the file is not a report (discovery leaves it to the lint to explain). The text reader and the lint read `layout=` and `tiles=` off the spelling, so it is grid. The SDK reader refuses to open it.

layoutCases.name: a query-level `# artifact` on a named query, with no model-level tag (deprecated)
layoutCases.knownDifference: The SDK reader opens only a file with a model-level `## artifact`, so a query-level report is not one to it.

layoutCases.name: a model-level tag naming no layout beside a query-level `# artifact`
layoutCases.knownDifference: The server's readers apply rule 2 (a query-level tag is grid); the SDK reader does not read query-level tags, so the model-level tag alone is linear by default.

layoutCases.name: a file with no artifact tag is no report
layoutCases.source: source: s is duckdb.sql("select 1 as x") extend { view: v is { group_by: x } }

queryTagCases.name: `# artifact` on a named query
`# artifact { … }` with properties on a named query
`# artifact` on a `run:` statement
queryTagCases.knownDifference: Compiled, only a named query's notes are read, so a tag on `run:` is no query-level tag; the text test and the lint read any `#` line.

queryTagCases.name: `# artifact` on a `source:` statement
queryTagCases.source:
# artifact
source: s is duckdb.sql("select 1 as x") extend { view: v is { group_by: x } }
queryTagCases.knownDifference: Compiled, only a named query's notes are read; the text test and the lint read any `#` line.

queryTagCases.name: `artifact` after another property on the line (`# title=x artifact`)
queryTagCases.knownDifference: The lint's test is `/^#\s*artifact\b/`, so it needs `artifact` first on the line; the compiled tag and the text test read it anywhere.

queryTagCases.name: `#artifact` with no space after the `#`
queryTagCases.knownDifference: Malloy does not read `#artifact` as an `artifact` tag and neither does the text test, which needs whitespace after the sigil; the lint's `/^#\s*artifact\b/` allows none.

queryTagCases.name: a quoted `"artifact"` is a string, not the tag
